dataset.question_policy: All original Russian test questions with nonempty paragraphs_uids.with_answer. No subsampling.
dataset.qrels_policy: Binary gain only for author-provided, crowd-verified with_answer IDs. Other IDs receive zero metric gain. No answer strings, SPARQL, related-ID lists or labels are supplied to the ranker.
dataset.corpus_policy: Every official paragraph, in release order. Only original paragraph text, one synthetic mailbox, unknown receipt dates. Fixed query date 2020-12-15.
dataset.primary: Macro nDCG@10, paired candidate minus baseline. Also macro known Recall@10, Hit@10, MRR@10 and counts of empty results for these positive questions.

bootstrap.unit: Transitive components of queries sharing a gold supporting Wikipedia page
bootstrap.estimator: Query-weighted paired percentile interval for nDCG@10 delta

entrypoint: Unmodified SearchEngine.search in separate local processes; shared passage vectors, each release's own query encoder.
limitations: Russian encyclopedic fact questions do not measure personal-mail retrieval, access control, RAG generation, or a VK leaderboard score.
Only selected candidate passages were manually judged by RuBQ annotators. Additional valid passages in the corpus may have zero measured gain. No verified-empty tasks are available.
Wikipedia paragraphs lack receipt dates. Each engine retains its normal handling of mail queries, including dates and identifiers. Candidate literal-quotation rules also remain active.
Pretraining overlap of the shared E5 model with public Wikipedia/RuBQ content was not audited.
